events.title: Dutch provinces renounce Philip II in the Act of Abjuration
events.description: The States General of the rebel provinces declared that Philip II had forfeited his rule by tyranny. The Act of Abjuration was in effect a declaration of independence for what became the Dutch Republic.
events.html: The States General of the rebel provinces declared that Philip II had forfeited his rule by tyranny. The Act of Abjuration was in effect a declaration of independence for what became the Dutch Republic.

events.title: First recorded women's cricket match is played in Surrey
events.description: Eleven women of Bramley played eleven of Hambledon on Gosden Common near Guildford, reported in the Reading Mercury. It is the earliest recorded women's cricket match.
events.html: Eleven women of Bramley played eleven of Hambledon on Gosden Common near Guildford, reported in the Reading Mercury. It is the earliest recorded women's cricket match.

events.title: Liberia declares independence
events.description: Liberia, founded by the American Colonization Society as a home for freed Black Americans, declared itself an independent republic. It became Africa's oldest modern republic, though settler rule marginalised indigenous peoples.
events.html: Liberia, founded by the American Colonization Society as a home for freed Black Americans, declared itself an independent republic. It became Africa's oldest modern republic, though settler rule marginalised indigenous peoples.

events.title: The Bureau of Investigation, forerunner of the FBI, is created
events.description: Attorney General Charles Bonaparte set up a force of special agents in the US Justice Department. Renamed the FBI in 1935, it grew under J. Edgar Hoover into America's main federal police agency.
events.html: Attorney General Charles Bonaparte set up a force of special agents in the US Justice Department. Renamed the FBI in 1935, it grew under J. Edgar Hoover into America's main federal police agency.

events.title: Fidel Castro leads the attack on the Moncada Barracks
events.description: Fidel Castro led some 160 rebels against the Moncada Barracks in Santiago de Cuba. The attack failed, but his trial speech 'History Will Absolve Me' made him a national figure, and 26 July named his movement.
events.html: Fidel Castro led some 160 rebels against the Moncada Barracks in Santiago de Cuba. The attack failed, but his trial speech 'History Will Absolve Me' made him a national figure, and 26 July named his movement.

events.title: Nasser nationalises the Suez Canal
events.description: Egypt's President Nasser announced the nationalisation of the Suez Canal Company to fund the Aswan Dam. Britain, France and Israel invaded in October, but US pressure forced a humiliating withdrawal.
